# Agent integration patches

Upstream base: `v0.5.0`, `55cd475b2e963fab32572606b95cc30ae9184568`.
The patches originated from unpublished working commit `10cf2d26f150a7d0bf7f88a7a4ed7fe362fd7698` on base `d66e1951613d1f95b145b65794370510fa8690bb`, then evolved in this repository. The release upgrade retains them; it does not enable Core orchestration or tool-call repair in the Agent.

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| aimux-core/src/error.rs | Round valid fractional Retry-After hints up to milliseconds so Agent retries cannot start early; reject negative/non-finite numeric hints. Regression: dim-agent-aimux/tests/model_flow/native.rs uses a real HTTP 25.1 ms hint. |
| aimux-core/src/parse_tool_call.rs | Export the existing JSON argument parser; preserve the native raw-string contract and existing parser behavior. |
| aimux-provider-utils/src/response_handler.rs | End the SSE stream at `[DONE]`, including when the HTTP connection stays open. |
| aimux-providers/src/openai/model.rs | Preserve absent usage, reject truncated or mixed-candidate streams and inconsistent tool identities/finish reasons; fix the first finish, allow usage tails, and reject generation after finish. Preserve refusal text as TextDelta. Do not emit complete tool calls for interrupted output. Accept `error: null` in initial chunks and throughout the stream while retaining actual provider errors. |
| aimux-providers/src/openai/types.rs | Read the choice index and refusal text used by the native stream contract. |
| aimux-provider-utils/src/http.rs | Allow an explicitly owned client per request and export the existing client builder; preserve the shared-client default for other callers. Remove raw URLs/header values from transport errors and redact URL credentials, query and fragment in diagnostics. |
| aimux-providers/src/openai/model.rs | Expose the same native stream pipeline with an optional caller-owned HTTP client; the existing entry point delegates with no override. |
| aimux-providers/src/openai/{convert.rs,convert_common.rs,responses/convert.rs} | Preserve explicitly selected service tiers for Chat and Responses, including model aliases. Remove the model-name tier whitelist; product catalog validation and remote account entitlement are the authorities. Regression: dim-agent-aimux/tests/model_flow/native.rs tests actual HTTP bodies for priority, flex, an unknown tier, and omission. |
| aimux-providers/src/openai/responses/convert.rs | Preserve explicit reasoning settings for deployment aliases instead of rejecting or dropping them based on model-name inference. Keep existing sampling and role heuristics unchanged. The same HTTP regression covers high, none, low, and omission. |
| aimux-providers/src/provider_registry.json | Use the SDK wire token-limit fields for DeepSeek, Moonshot, Aihubmix and Zenmux Chat presets instead of inferring the field from model names. Moonshot uses max_completion_tokens; the others use max_tokens. Regression: dim-app-server/tests/provider_flow.rs exercises selection through actual HTTP execution. |
| aimux-providers/src/openai/responses/mod.rs | Omit Authorization when the native config has no API key. Request-local custom auth (including Azure api-key) must not be accompanied by an empty Bearer header. Regression: dim-app-server/tests/provider_flow.rs exercises Azure admission and actual Responses HTTP. |
| aimux-providers/src/{anthropic,google}/model.rs | Omit absent default API-key headers, preserving explicit anonymous/custom authentication from the resolved connection. Regression: dim-agent-aimux/tests/model_flow/native.rs checks actual HTTP headers alongside nonempty key and bearer cases. |
| aimux-providers/src/xai/{model.rs,types.rs,responses/mod.rs} | Inject the caller-owned client, preserve endpoint queries and omit empty default auth. Reuse the shared JSON header builder. Chat streaming consumes only choice index 0 (also the default for an omitted index), ignoring other choices. It preserves repeated deltas and ordered reasoning/text blocks, validates tool identities and explicit finish evidence, and retains usage tails without fabricating usage. Responses validates streamed function identity/arguments, preserves function item IDs, content-part indices and encrypted reasoning, rejects missing terminal/unfinished output, and never promotes a failed terminal to tool success. Delta and done events use the same message content-part identity, so done-only parts remain ordered without replaying completed delta parts. It ends at the terminal without waiting for HTTP EOF. Regressions: native_protocol_metadata_test.rs plus Agent model_flow and product provider_flow. |
| aimux-providers/src/bedrock/* and direct signer callers | Use official aws-sigv4 1.6.0 with explicit credentials and exact body bytes; reject reserved header overrides. Bedrock Converse encodes model IDs as one path segment, uses a caller-owned client and incrementally decodes CRC-checked, 16 MiB-bounded frames with aws-smithy-eventstream 0.61.4. It rejects malformed, exceptional, truncated, unsupported, or unterminated streams and finishes at trailing metadata without waiting for HTTP EOF. Request maxTokens remains the exact caller limit, topK is not put in common inferenceConfig, tool errors retain status, and Bedrock reasoning continuation metadata is replayed. The AWS crates raise the vendored provider package's effective local MSRV from 1.85 to 1.94.1 (the repository toolchain is 1.98.1). |
| aimux-provider-utils/src/http.rs | Byte bodies preserve an explicitly supplied Content-Type instead of appending a second value, matching the existing JSON body behavior and keeping signed headers identical to wire headers. |
| aimux-core/src/error.rs; provider error producers | Add the serialized `ApiCallErrorOrigin` fact (`transport`, `httpResponse`, `streamEvent`, `local`; legacy input defaults to `unknown`) and require every internal `ApiCallError::new` caller to select one. HTTP send/body transport, complete responses, provider stream events, and local construction are marked at their actual construction boundary; origin is never inferred from status or response-body presence. |

Anthropic Messages, Google GenerateContent, and OpenAI Responses models accept a caller-owned client via `.with_client`. All their generate/stream paths propagate it through `HttpRequest`; callers without an override retain the shared-client behavior. GoogleModel is exported through the existing google module. The Agent adapter injects its process plugin's client for every protocol, so unloading releases the pool after requests and native streams settle.

Native continuation patches preserve Anthropic signature-only and redacted thinking blocks, Gemini signed Part boundaries (including empty parts), and Responses item IDs, encrypted content, summary indices, multiple text parts, and phase. Responses replay groups parts from the same item without duplicate IDs. Anthropic/Gemini/Responses endpoints preserve existing query parameters; Gemini appends streamGenerateContent with an encoded model ID and alt=sse.

xAI Responses reasoning text and summary deltas share the same item-opening path. A missing or late summary-part-added event cannot emit a delta before its native start or reset accumulated text. The Agent continuation flow verifies exact text and encrypted metadata through replay.

xAI Responses error terminals preserve the provider message and code through the existing API error conversion. Both `response.failed` and a failed `response.done` stop the stream, as does an `error` event; none emits a second EOF error or a Finish. xAI Chat likewise stops at an in-band provider error without flushing an additional terminal result, but accepts `error: null` in the first chunk, later chunks and usage tails. The native HTTP flows cover null errors and partial output followed by each actual error shape.

Native streams require the protocol's terminal evidence: Responses completed/incomplete/failed events, Anthropic message_stop with a stop reason, and Gemini candidate finishReason. Gemini and Vertex finish after processing that terminal chunk's content, usage, and metadata, even while the HTTP body stays open. Early EOF returns InvalidResponseData without a successful Finish, even when complete tool calls were received. The checks apply to the shared OpenAI/Azure/Codex Responses reducer, shared Anthropic/AWS core, and both Vertex streaming parsers. Provider errors and incomplete or filtered output remain failures. Responses emits refusal.delta and refusal.done as visible text, suppresses the done copy after deltas, and preserves refusal text in non-streaming results. Gemini closes preceding text or reasoning before a functionCall so subsequent content starts a distinct block and replay preserves its position.

Inline image/file conversion uses the existing ContentPart variants: Responses emits input_image for image MIME types; Google/Vertex emits inlineData for base64 and fileData for URLs. Google thinkingConfig is retained in generationConfig. Chat, Responses and Google header builders add Content-Type only when no case-insensitive explicit value exists; the adapter follows each native authentication header spelling and merges configured headers once.

Bedrock rejects URL media before issuing HTTP instead of silently dropping it. Inline image bytes remain supported; the Agent Bedrock flow verifies the exact image payload and that rejected URLs issue no request for either bearer or SigV4 authentication.

The patches do not add timeouts, retries, repair, or new model configuration fields. Bedrock bounds its binary frame buffer; OpenAI-compatible providers retain the Chat implementation. Bedrock unsigned reasoning is valid and remains visible, but is not replayed, matching the TS adapter. Signed reasoning and decoded/re-encoded redacted byte fragments preserve continuation. Completed tool calls are withheld until a matching terminal and usage metadata are received; malformed or interrupted output cannot complete a tool call. The official signer needs both `sign-http` and `http1` in v1.6.0; removing `http1` fails to compile its HTTP implementation.

Public protocol regression flows: `aimux-providers/tests/openai_native_contract_test.rs`, `aimux-providers/tests/native_protocol_metadata_test.rs`, and `aimux-providers/tests/bedrock_native_flow_test.rs`.
All are registered as test targets of `dim-agent-aimux`, so the normal workspace test command covers the patch. Run from `rust/`:

```sh
cargo test --offline -p dim-agent-aimux --test aimux_native_contract --test aimux_native_protocol_metadata
cargo test --offline -p dim-agent-aimux --test aimux_bedrock_native_flow
cargo test --offline -p dim-agent-aimux --test model_flow native
```

Before vendoring, 198 related upstream tests passed (OpenAI, native stream, Groq, Azure, DeepSeek, tool argument parsing, HTTP helpers). After fixing finish and refusal handling, 173 affected provider tests passed, including 12 native contract tests. The changed crates and native regression tests passed Clippy with warnings denied.
